pr.title: Async drop codegen
pr.author: azhogin

analysis.originalLogic: Before this rework, coroutine drop elaboration only rewrote a plain `TerminatorKind::Drop` for `SELF_ARG`, and StateTransform only asserted that no sync coroutine drop shim existed (`assert!(body.coroutine_drop().is_none());`) before transforming the async context. The PR describes the old async drop glue as an implementation “using mixing language-level futures”, then replaces it with `elaborate_drops::elaborate_drop` plus `coroutine::StateTransform`. The new logic distinguishes normal drops from possible async drops: `build_drop` creates a `Pin::new_unchecked(&mut place)` -> `AsyncDrop::drop`/`async_drop_in_place` call -> `Drop { async_fut: Some(fut) }` chain only when the feature is enabled, the enclosing body is a coroutine, async drops are allowed, the block is not cleanup, and the dropped type `needs_async_drop`. Nested drop ladders thread a separate `dropline` successor so a suspended coroutine can later poll the same async-drop future.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: A transform that leaves such a `Drop` as an ordinary sync drop with `drop: None, async_fut: None`, or that discards the hidden `drop`/`async_fut` successors when rebuilding the terminator, is wrong: it calls the synchronous destructor instead of running/awaiting `AsyncDrop`, and loses the path used when the coroutine is dropped after the drop future has been created. Equally incorrect is emitting the async-drop ladder when `block.is_cleanup`/`unwind.is_cleanup()` is true: cleanup paths must remain synchronous. The corrected transform gates async drop on non-cleanup coroutine blocks, builds the pin/call/future chain, preserves `dropline`, and later lets StateTransform expand those hidden drops into yield/poll states.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust async functions/coroutines compiled with `#![feature(async_drop)]` where a local whose type needs async drop goes out of scope. The domain includes direct `AsyncDrop` types, nested structs/enums/arrays/slices, coroutines suspended mid-execution, and the coroutine itself being async-dropped. A control program can use the same scope structure but a sync-only type or `ManuallyDrop`, isolating the async-drop transformation. The PR's regression tests also cover the unresumed case, a suspended coroutine (`MiddleFuture`), nested futures, moved-out fields, arrays, generics, enums, and unions.
analysis.summary: Async drop codegen reworked coroutine drop elaboration so async-droppable places produce a pinned async-drop future and a dropline ladder, then StateTransform expands those hidden drops into yield/poll states. It is a feature rework that also fixes confirmed ICEs; the reusable correctness rule is to preserve the new drop/async_fut successors and never turn cleanup-path drops into async drops.
analysis.trigger: StateTransform runs on a coroutine body containing `TerminatorKind::Drop` for an async-droppable local, and ElaborateDrops builds the drop ladder for that terminator.
preconditions: The crate enables the unstable `async_drop` feature.
The enclosing MIR body is a coroutine (`body.coroutine.is_some()`).
The drop is on a non-cleanup path; cleanup/unwind drops must stay sync.
`allow_async_drops()` is true for the elaborator and the dropped type `needs_async_drop`.
For StateTransform expansion, the coroutine is async/async-gen and `has_expandable_async_drops` is true.
Any pass cloning or reconstructing `TerminatorKind::Drop` preserves the hidden `drop` and `async_fut` fields.
pitfalls: Do not generate an async drop inside a cleanup block or a cleanup drop ladder; the patch asserts `Dropline is set for cleanup drop ladder` if this invariant is violated.
Do not drop `async_fut` or `drop` while rebuilding a `Drop` terminator; otherwise the later poll/yield expansion and dropline successor disappear.
An async drop is a hidden yield and therefore needs the same dropline preparation as a `Yield` terminator.
For an unresumed coroutine with async drops, the clean-drop shim must return `Poll::Ready(())` rather than the sync-only `Return`.
Dropping a coroutine after its async drop has started must not resume normal execution as if it were still running; the resume path after the drop yield goes to a panic block (`ResumedAfterDrop`).
analysis.testStrategy: Use `//@ run-pass` plus `//@ check-run-results` tests with a deterministic `block_on` that polls a pinned future to completion and then calls `unsafe { async_drop_in_place(fut.get_unchecked_mut()) }`, polling that drop future to completion. Assert exact stdout ordering for active fields, nested ADTs, and mid-execution drops (`async-drop-middle-drop`, `async-drop-open`, `async-drop-future-from-future`). Include a suspended coroutine with an async-droppable local and verify that dropping it invokes `AsyncDrop` rather than sync `Drop`. Run `tests/ui/async-await/async-drop/ex-ice-132103.rs` with `-Zvalidate-mir -Zinline-mir=yes`; it was moved from a known-bug crash test to run-pass.
evidence: Scopes processing for generate async drop preparations. Async drop is a hidden Yield, so potentially async drops require the same dropline preparation as for Yield terminators.
Drops in unwind path (cleanup blocks) are not expanded to async drops, only sync drops in unwind path
Dropline is set for cleanup drop ladder

AsyncDropGlue shim generation uses `elaborate_drops::elaborate_drop` to produce drop ladder (in the similar way as for sync drop glue) and then `coroutine::StateTransform` to convert function into coroutine poll.
This test used to ICE: rust-lang/rust#132103
Fixed when re-work async drop to shim drop glue coroutine scheme.
